tb21_profile.skill: Design a biological sequence that simultaneously satisfies many interacting hard constraints: pick proteins by spectral/ligand-binding criteria from external databases (PDB, FPbase), parse FASTA and GenBank, order subdomains, trim N-terminal methionines, reverse-translate to DNA and keep windowed GC in range
tb21_profile.domain: Molecular biology / synthetic biology: FASTA, GenBank plasmids, PDB entries, FRET fluorescent proteins, GS linkers, codon usage and GC content
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec constraint-satisfaction design, verified by re-checking every stated constraint on one output file

verifier_notes: The packet's verifier field and work/verifier_strength.json disagree on ~27% of shown candidates pool-wide (845 of them involve a FREE/non-FREE flip), so I excluded from final_top10 anything graded FREE by either source. Affected here: TerminalWorld tw_1025 and tw_338534 are FREE in the packet but 'ok' in verifier_strength.json - I kept them in per_source only and did not promote them. CalibForge scientific-computing_20260414_080620_004 (restriction digest fragment prediction) is FREE in the packet and excluded everywhere despite good domain fit; its sibling scientific-computing_20260422_235114_003 covers the same ground with a strong verifier. TMax task_000836_100fba26 is 'ok' in the packet and 'behavioral' in verifier_strength.json; reading the instruction, the held-out check runs the classifier script over clean/evil corpora and compares exit codes, which is a real behavioural test, so I kept it in final_top10.

Remove restriction sites from a synthesized gene by synonymous substitution without changing the encoded protein; exactly the codon-swap manoeuvre a GC-window fix needs.
Scan circular plasmid GenBank files on both strands for ORFs and emit FASTA; the GenBank-plus-FASTA parsing this task needs for plasmid.gb and antibody.fasta.
Pick protein structures suitable for a competitive ligand-binding assay; choosing a protein by what small molecule it binds is exactly the SMILES-to-binder step here.
Analyse circular plasmid GenBank records where genes wrap the origin; careful coordinate and strand handling in the same file format as plasmid.gb.
Fix a DNA-to-protein translator that mishandles NCBI genetic-code tables; the codon table correctness the gBlock depends on, inverted.
Decide exactly which proteins in a proteome are kinases given reference catalytic domains; identifying a protein from sequence evidence, as with the antibody's target.
Extract binding thermodynamics for methotrexate binding to DHFR from raw ITC traces; the same protein and ligand-binding subject, but a data-reduction task.
Repair GROMACS-mangled PDB records back to the column-exact PDB spec; strict structural-file format discipline of the kind PDB lookups require.

notes: CalibForge is far and away the best pool for this task and takes 8 of the 10 final slots. Its scientific-computing_*_003/004/006 family is real synthetic-biology work - codon optimization under multiple hard constraints, restriction-site removal, circular-plasmid GenBank parsing, PDB format conformance, ligand-binding assay design - and it is well verified (nearly all strong). One CalibForge item is worth flagging to the merge step for a different reason: scientific-computing_20260607_104421_006 is an ITC analysis of methotrexate binding to DHFR, i.e. literally the same protein and ligand family as this TB2.1 task, but the work is curve fitting, so I ranked it 9th within CalibForge and left it out of the final ten; if subject-matter overlap is being weighted it is the obvious swap-in. Gap nothing in the pool covers: this task requires live calls to the PDB and FPbase REST APIs and reading spectral metadata back. No candidate in any of the seven corpora does network-API-driven scientific lookup; the nearest are Terminal-Lego task_14837 (chained web fetches) and TerminalWorld tw_338534 (download Swiss-Prot), both weak and the latter FREE. Terminal-Lego and TerminalWorld have almost no biology: Terminal-Lego yielded four DNA-adjacent items at most (task_08980, task_09030) and its list below rank 4 is honest filler; Recursive-Task-Synthesis has three (wgsim, two refgenie) and then nothing, so ranks 4-10 there are generic constraint-conformance tasks scoring 1-2. SWE-Smith has zero biology. Neither new corpus is weak here - Terminal-Lego is, CalibForge is the best in the pool - so the two new corpora clearly beat the old ones for this task.
